Name: Notepad++
Description: The vendor's NSIS installer, wrapped with the vendor uninstaller wired to uninstall and to rollback.
Awkwardness: The whole difficulty is one NSIS quirk: /D= must be the last switch on the line and must not be quoted, even when the target path contains spaces. /S /D="C:\Program Files\Notepad++" looks correct, is accepted without complaint, and installs to the default location anyway - so a fleet ends up with the application somewhere other than where the detection rule looks. Notepad++ also releases often enough that the wrapped installer's file name changes constantly, and the 32-bit and 64-bit downloads are named almost identically, so the wrong one lands in Program Files (x86) and every path-based rule written for it misses.
SetupFileHint: npp.X.Y.Z.Installer.x64.exe - check you took the x64 build, not the x86 one.
Notes: NOT tested in this repository. /S for NSIS is about as well established as a silent switch gets, but nothing here has been run against a real device.
Run 'msimaker analyze <installer>' against your download to confirm the NSIS fingerprint.
/D= is deliberately unquoted. Do not add quotes: NSIS takes the rest of the line verbatim and quoting it silently breaks the switch.

The uninstall command assumes the vendor uninstaller is uninstall.exe in the install folder. Confirm the file name on a test device before relying on it - an uninstall action pointing at a file that does not exist is a package that cannot be removed.
Set Version to the Notepad++ version you downloaded.

Arp.Comments: Notepad++ wrapped as an MSI. Silent switches from vendor documentation, untested.
